added_failures_note: derived from the reviewed run's own gate logs: baseline_suite at b8cc7f0f6 (baseline.log, 15 passed, exit 0, failure_ids []) minus after_suite at 5af5e8561 (gate.log, 19 passed, exit 0, failure_ids []); no failure id in the head arm is read from the base arm

findings.text: _target_shape (placement.py:500) re-implements the job-shape read that reckon/crew/fleet_node.py:254 fleet_node.allocation_shape already owns and that placement.py:732 already calls to read a job's partition, cores and memory; _read_target_job (placement.py:440) likewise re-derives the one-job state query and its 'empty answer vs unreadable question' distinction that reckon/crew/runs.py:4308 scheduler_job_state and runs.py:4193 _ask_scheduler own, and the record assembly at placement.py:583 repeats the block placement.py:740 _adopt_live_fleet_allocation already builds for a job read from the scheduler. The addition duplicates all three owners without extending any; the atomic single-query reason in the docstring (placement.py:76-79) justifies one combined reader, not the re-derivation of an owned shape parse and state read.

the fake scheduler answers an unknown job id with empty stdout and exit 0, but this cluster's `squeue -h -j 99999999 -o '%T|%u|%P|%c|%m'` exits 1 with "slurm_load_jobs error: Invalid job id specified" on stderr, so in production _read_target_job (placement.py:464) takes the non-zero-exit branch and raises the 'could not be asked about job 99999999' refusal, never the "does not know job 99999999" text line 362 asserts, which is unreachable for Slurm. I reproduced both: the real call returned the could-not-be-asked message, and the fake's empty-stdout/exit-0 shape is what makes the assertion pass. The done-when's third refusal case is therefore exercised only against a scheduler behaviour the deployment target does not exhibit; the refusal itself still fires and the record is left untouched.

justifications.durability: I reproduced the declared negative control: making _replacement_refusal admit a pending target reddens test_replacement_refuses_a_pending_job (1 failed, EXIT=1, DID NOT RAISE CrewError), a test the head arm passes, so the pending guard is real; but test_replacement_refuses_a_job_the_scheduler_does_not_know guards a branch production never reaches, so it cannot redden on a production regression.
justifications.evidence: the gate tests/test_crew_placement_reservation.py together with tests/test_ensure_holds_one_reservation.py is green at 19 passed exit 0, which I reproduced at head (base 15 passed): but the third done-when refusal case is asserted only against a fake whose answer this cluster's squeue does not give, so the gate does not measure that case's production behaviour.
justifications.fit: the added names at placement.py:80-85, :430-547 are mechanism names REPLACEMENT_JOB_QUERY... (REPLACEMENT_JOB_QUERY, _read_target_job, _replacement_refusal) with no plan, ticket or version id and no attribution, and the comments state mechanism; the one slip is _replacement_owner (placement.py:435) re-wording the user resolution fleet_node.py:192 already carries.
justifications.goal_fidelity: placement.py:547 replace_reservation names the target explicitly, refuses pending / other-user / unknown-id through _replacement_refusal (placement.py:521), records the replaced id (placement.py:583 "replaced") and prints both (placement.py:596-608), and dispatch.py:9025 places the new job, so every later dispatch and resume moves while running steps are untouched.
justifications.reuse: the change reuses publish_reservation, read_reservation, _reservation_hold_lock, reservation_options, _roster_reach and fleet_node.parse_memory_gb, but _target_shape (placement.py:500) and _read_target_job (placement.py:440) re-implement the shape read owned by fleet_node.allocation_shape and the state read owned by runs.scheduler_job_state rather than extending either, and rebuild the record assembly placement.py:740 owns, so the dimension scores at the re-implementation cap.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --stat b8cc7f0f6..5af5e8561 lists exactly reckon/crew/placement.py, reckon/cli.py, tests/test_crew_placement_reservation.py and the evidence fragment, the four files the manifest declares, and nothing else.
